subhead: Four terms on your benefits summary shape most of what you pay. Here’s how they work, then follow one employee’s year to see them in action.

section1.title: The four terms to know first
section1.lead: You’ll see them on every benefits summary. Here’s what each one actually means for your wallet.

cards.label: Deductible
cards.title: Your entry fee
cards.body: What you pay each plan year before your plan starts splitting the cost of care.

cards.label: Copay
cards.title: The flat fee
cards.body: A set price for common services, like $30 for an office visit or $15 for a generic prescription.

cards.label: Coinsurance
cards.title: Your share of the tab
cards.body: After the deductible, you pay a percentage, like 20%, and the plan covers the rest.

cards.label: Out-of-pocket max
cards.title: Your safety net
cards.body: The most you’ll pay in a plan year for covered in-network care. Hit it, and the plan pays 100%.

story.title: Follow one employee’s year
story.intro: Jordan’s plan has a $1,500 deductible, 20% coinsurance, a $30 office copay, and a $4,000 out-of-pocket max. All care is in network.

timeline.detail: 20% would be $800, but Jordan hits the max first.
The plan pays 100% of covered in-network care.

stats.label: The plan paid
stats.desc: for the surgery and MRI alone

headsUp.title: Heads up: these don’t count toward your max

items.title: Premiums
items.body: The amount taken from your paycheck for coverage.

items.title: Non-covered care
items.body: Services your plan excludes, like most cosmetic procedures.

items.title: Out-of-network extras
items.body: May have a separate limit, plus any amount billed above what your plan allows.

steps.text: Your Summary of Benefits and Coverage lists them all.
Out-of-network care may have a higher limit, or none.
Most plans cover in-network checkups and screenings at $0.
Check prior authorization, and whether an HSA or FSA can help.

contact.title: Need help? Call Atria.
contact.body: Stuck on a claim, a surprise bill, or a coverage question? Our team will work through it with you.

disclaimer: *On many plans, copays don’t count toward the deductible but do count toward the out-of-pocket max; high-deductible plans work differently. Figures are illustrative. For informational purposes only; not legal or tax advice.
